title: Adjoining a coherent inverse to an already invertible arrow preserves simplicial categories
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and their path-component categories $\pi_0$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], with the Bergner model structure whose weak equivalences are the Dwyer--Kan equivalences of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. A cofibration has the left lifting property against all trivial fibrations, and trivial means also a weak equivalence. Let $A$ be the discrete simplicial category with objects $0,1$ and one nonidentity arrow $a:0\to1$. Let $\mathbb J$ be the discrete simplicial category with these two objects and exactly one arrow for each ordered pair, and let $i:A\to\mathbb J$ carry $a$ to its distinguished isomorphism. Choose any factorization $A\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}\mathbb J$ of $i$ with $j$ a cofibration and $q$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. For every small simplicial category $C$ and every simplicial functor $f:A\to C$ for which $[f(a)]$ is invertible in $\pi_0C$, the canonical map
$$C\longrightarrow C\amalg_A E$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and a cofibration. The pushout is the ordinary pushout of simplicial categories. No cofibration hypothesis on $f$, no local Kan hypothesis on $C$, and no requirement that $f(0)$ and $f(1)$ be distinct are imposed.

source.place: HTT Definition A.3.2.12, Remark A.3.2.14 (the reformulation with a cofibrant replacement), and Example A.3.2.18, printed pp. 862-863. Read online 2026-10-17. WANTED: archival HTT in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category theorem.

proof.text: Work first with the fixed object set $O=\{0,1\}$. The walking arrow $A$ is cofibrant there: adjoin its single degree-zero arrow to the identity-only category, a free boundary cell. Factor $A\to\mathbb J$ as $j_0:A\to E_0$ a fixed-object cofibration and $q_0:E_0\to\mathbb J$ a fixed-object trivial fibration, using [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. Thus $E_0$ is cofibrant and all four mapping sets are weakly contractible. These are also a Bergner cofibration and trivial fibration. Indeed the square against a free boundary generator $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ is exactly a boundary lifting square on the selected mapping set; the empty-to-singleton generator tests object-surjectivity. Hence $q_0$ is $I$-injective. Conversely a Bergner trivial fibration has mappingwise trivial fibrations by these squares. A fixed-object cofibration lifts against it after replacing its source and target by the two labelled mapping categories selected by the square. This proves the claimed Bergner cofibration assertion for $j_0$, including squares whose two labelled objects have the same image.

source.place: Sections 7.2 and 7.6; fixed-object factorization and the elementary generating-square correspondence

proof.text: The square with top $j_0:A\to E_0$, bottom $q:E\to\mathbb J$, left $j$ and right $q_0$ has a lift $t:E\to E_0$ with $tj=j_0$ and $q_0t=q$. Two-out-of-three makes $t$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Both $E$ and $E_0$ are cofibrant objects of the undercategory $A/\mathrm{sCat}$, whose model classes are those on the underlying arrows. Cobase change $F=C\amalg_A(-):A/\mathrm{sCat}\to C/\mathrm{sCat}$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by lifting-class pushout closure [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to $t$: write $t=pi$ with $p$ a trivial fibration and a cofibration section $s$ satisfying $ps=1$. Since $p$ and $t$ are weak equivalences, both $i$ and $s$ are trivial cofibrations. Thus $F(i)$ and $F(s)$ are weak equivalences; $F(p)F(s)=1$ makes $F(p)$ a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Consequently $F(t):C\amalg_A E\to C\amalg_A E_0$ is a weak equivalence, commuting with the two maps from $C$. It suffices to prove the result for $E_0$.

source.place: HTT Remark A.3.2.14: independence of cofibrant inverse-adjunction choice; explicit undercategory split-factorization argument

proof.text: Form the two-labelled category $D$ with $D(i,k)=C(f(i),f(k))$, even when $f(0)=f(1)$, and use the vertex $f(a)$ in $D(0,1)$. Its class is invertible by assumption. [lem-coef-countable-equivalence-witness] gives $A\to H\to D$ preserving the specified vertex, with all four mapping sets of $H$ weakly contractible. In the fixed-object model factor $A\to H$ as a cofibration $A\to K$ followed by a trivial fibration $K\to H$ [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. Then $K$ is cofibrant, all four of its mapping sets are weakly contractible, and the composite $K\to H\to D\to C$ extends the original $f$ exactly. Neither the witness nor this factorization requires Kan mapping sets.

source.place: Bergner Lemma 2.4 and Section 4; relative fixed-object factorization

proof.text: Put $P=K\amalg_A E_0$ in the fixed-object category. Its map from $K$ is a cofibration, so $P$ is cofibrant. Both $\pi_0K$ and $\pi_0E_0$ are the two-object groupoid $\mathbb J$, since their four mapping sets are nonempty and weakly contractible. The functor $\pi_0$ is left adjoint to discrete enrichment: a simplicial functor into a discrete category is precisely a functor out of the path-component category. It therefore preserves this pushout. Thus $\pi_0P=\mathbb J\amalg_{[1]}\mathbb J\cong\mathbb J$: the common distinguished arrow has a unique inverse, forcing the two inverse arrows to agree. In particular both $K$ and $P$ satisfy the groupoid hypothesis of the nerve-detection lemma.

source.place: Sections 7.2 and 10.1; explicit path-component pushout calculation

proof.text: Use the diagonal classifying nerve $N$ defined in [lem-coef-cofibrant-localization-diagonal-nerve]. Since degreewise groupoid completion of the walking arrow is $\mathbb J$, the ordinary pushout $L=K\amalg_A\mathbb J$ is precisely $K[A^{-1}]$. The map $A\to K$ is a cofibration between cofibrant objects in the fixed-object model. Apply [lem-coef-cofibrant-localization-diagonal-nerve] with $V=A$ and $B=K$ to obtain a weak homotopy equivalence $NK\to NL$. This assertion concerns diagonal nerves, not enriched mapping sets, and requires no invertibility hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 10.2, printed p.281; specialization to the walking-arrow subcategory

proof.text: The comparison $r:P\to L$ is the pushout of $q_0:E_0\to\mathbb J$ along $E_0\to P$. The latter is a cofibration, being the pushout of $A\to K$. Since $q_0$ is a mappingwise weak equivalence, fixed-object left properness [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-left-proper] makes $r$ a mappingwise weak equivalence. To pass to nerves, in nerve degree $p$ the map is the coproduct, indexed by the same strings of objects, of the products of the corresponding $p$ mapping-set maps. Realization preserves coproducts and finite products by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Homotopy groups of a finite product are the products of the homotopy groups (a based map or homotopy into a product is a tuple), and a path or a connected sphere stays in one coproduct summand. These row maps are therefore weak homotopy equivalences, including the empty product when $p=0$. [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] gives that $Nr:NP\to NL$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 7.3(ii), Section 1.4(vi)–(vii); explicit finite-product and disjoint-union row calculation

proof.text: The composite $NK\to NP\to NL$ is the weak equivalence of step 5, and its second map is a weak equivalence by step 6. Hence $NK\to NP$ is a weak equivalence. The categories $K$ and $P$ are cofibrant on the same set $O$ and both have groupoidal path-component categories by step 4. Apply [lem-coef-groupoidal-cofibrant-nerve-detection] to conclude that $K\to P$ is a mappingwise weak equivalence. It is already a fixed-object cofibration, so is a fixed-object trivial cofibration.

A fixed-object trivial cofibration $K\to P$ has the left lifting property against every $J$-injective functor $X\to Y$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For a lifting square, fix the object labels given by its top map. On those labels $X(i,k)\to Y(i,k)$ is a Kan fibration, by the characterization of $J$-injective maps in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. The fixed-object trivial cofibration lifts against this labelled fixed-object fibration by [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. Composing the resulting labelled lift with $X$ solves the original square. By pushout closure of the left lifting class [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], its pushout along $K\to C$ also lifts against every $J$-injective map, so lies in $J\text{-cof}$. Every $J\text{-cof}$ map is a retract of a relative $J\text{-cell}$ map [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]; relative $J\text{-cell}$ maps are Dwyer--Kan equivalences and these are closed under retracts [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. Hence this pushout is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The pushout is $C\to C\amalg_KP\cong C\amalg_A E_0$: a functor out of either displayed target is precisely a pair of functors from $C$ and $E_0$ agreeing on $A$. A fixed-object pushout of identity-on-object functors is also a pushout with arbitrary target object functions by the same labelled-target argument. No injectivity of the object function $K\to C$ is needed.

source.place: Fixed-object lifting, Section 7.2; HTT Remark A.3.2.14, ordinary cobase change

proof.text: By step 2 the map $C\amalg_A E\to C\amalg_A E_0$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and its composite with $C\to C\amalg_A E$ is the equivalence proved in step 8. Two-out-of-three [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability] proves that $C\to C\amalg_A E$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. It is a cofibration because it is the pushout of the given cofibration $j$, by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. This establishes both conclusions for the original, arbitrary factorization $E$.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-81e0599db (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all nine steps, both new nodes and every cited statement. No cycles: none of the item's 11 dependencies reaches the item. The statement is unchanged and agrees with HTT A.3.2.14.

One fault (C1/C2), in step 8, repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-simplicial-invertible-arrow-pushout.json. The step concluded 'Bergner trivial cofibration', which step 9 uses as a DK equivalence, without citing why. It was also marked elementary. The repaired step shows that K→P lifts against every J-injective map, using interval-lifting's characterization. By pushout closure, C→C⊔_A E0 is then in J-cof. A J-cof map is a retract of a J-cell map (interval-lifting), and J-cell maps are DK equivalences, closed under retracts (cell-stability). The step now uses cell-stability and is no longer elementary; proof_deps is unchanged.

Other steps:
- Step 1: j0 and q0 are Bergner maps by the labelled argument, which also covers u(0)=u(1).
- Step 2: the lift t exists; Brown's lemma in A/sCat is correct, with C⊔_A(−) acting as cobase change.
- Step 3: two labels satisfy the witness node even when f(0)=f(1); the factorization A→K→H avoids assuming A→H is a cofibration.
- Step 4: π0P = J⊔_[1]J = J, because [1]→J is an epimorphism.
- Step 5: G(A)=J, so L=K[A^{-1}].
- Step 6: left properness is applied on the correct leg (E0→P is a cofibration), then a row argument and the diagonal lemma.
- Step 7: cofibrancy and groupoidal π0 are checked for K and P; L is correctly not used.
- Step 9: two-out-of-three plus cobase change of j.

New nodes (DK 9.6 and DK 10.2):
- Both are self-contained, statement-only and true. I checked them independently; for 9.6 the key input is Ω_x N ≃ U(x,x) for grouplike π0. Tested on O empty, the walking arrow (Δ¹ against NJ) and the free monoid (BN ≃ BZ ≃ S¹).
- Neither duplicates DK 9.2/9.5, cofibrant-simplicial-inversion (which is cyclic) or free-category-groupoid-nerve, and neither restates a clause of the item.
- Their numbering agrees with the existing DK nodes. Searches and the blueprint ancestor are correct.

- The Bergner model-structure axioms Brown needs in step 2 come from the statement's existing context, the same convention as its parents; no independent node states them.
